correctness.rationale: For q>=3, m>=1 and every word with y_i unequal to y_j for 1<=|i-j|<=2, the candidate position sets S_i={j in {i,i+1,i+2}:x_j=y_i} are pairwise disjoint and their total size is at most m+2; positive embeddings require each nonempty. The two possible surplus positions force at most four embeddings. The c_i=3 and two c=2 cases give exactly 2m-1 multiplicity-three hosts and binomial(m,2) multiplicity-four hosts; T=q^2 binomial(m+2,2) and S=sum_{j=0}^2 binomial(m+2,j)(q-1)^j give all other counts. Posterior probabilities are e_y(x)/T. Full-host DP and insertion-history algorithms independently passed the documented finite test grid (1226 patterns, 513126 histories, 484024 direct DP evaluations). No argument uses a finite cutoff as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The object is the natural posterior input multiplicity distribution after exactly two deletions, specialized to a structurally motivated locally rainbow family (all contiguous triples pairwise distinct). The all-length, all-q>=3 theorem provides exact N0..N4, proves sharp bounded maximal embedding multiplicity, identifies the precise high-multiplicity configurations and yields an explicit channel entropy formula and asymptotic correction 4/q. This is neither a trivial first-moment calculation nor a single arbitrary finite slice. It does not assert global entropy maximization.
